## Overview **+2.7% to +4.7% decode at c=1 on SPEED-Bench over the best fixed draft depth** (11 categories, four same-node runs, mean about +3.7%), within noise at c=4, GSM8K within run-to-run noise, on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP, one DGX Spark (SM121), with the NVFP4 draft head from #59973. Opt-in. While one request is decoding, `draft_confidence_threshold` turns `num_speculative_tokens` into a maximum depth: drafting stops once the drafter's top-1 probability falls below the threshold (the first draft is always kept), and only the drafted prefix is verified, using FULL CUDA graphs captured per verify length for a single request, as Dynamic SD (#32374) does per K. With more than one request the stop is off and the speculator drafts and verifies `draft_confidence_fallback_depth` tokens, with no readback. The stop reads only the drafter's distributions, never the drawn tokens, so rejection sampling stays exact. ```bash vllm serve --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 6, "draft_confidence_threshold": 0.6, "draft_confidence_fallback_depth": 3}' ``` Model Runner V2, MTP/EAGLE/EAGLE3, SM121 only; any other configuration is rejected at startup. ## Results SPEED-Bench qualitative (32 prompts per category, greedy, 256 tokens), Flash-Next NVFP4, #59973 NVFP4 draft head, BF16 KV, both arms on one GB10 node (median SM clock 2522 MHz), one run per arm, measured on the final commit 7c4775ff31. Fixed 3 is the best fixed depth: in two other same-node sweeps fixed 4 was 0.1% and 0.6% slower, and on another node fixed 6 was 6.6% slower than fixed 3. | | fixed 3 drafts | confidence stop (max 6, fallback 3) | delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | decode c=1, 11 categories | 49.1 tok/s (AL 2.80) | 50.5 tok/s (AL 3.07) | **+2.7%** | | decode c=4, 6 categories, per request | 33.0 tok/s | 32.6 tok/s | -1.2% | Per category at c=1: coding +16.7%, rag +9.0%, math +4.2%, multilingual +2.8%, writing +1.8%, roleplay +0.9%, qa +0.8%, reasoning +0.0%, stem -2.0%, humanities -2.1%, **summarization -7.7%**. Disclaimers: - Run to run spread is about 2%. Same-node c=1 runs of earlier commits with the same stop logic gave +4.4%, +2.9% and +4.7%; c=4 ranged from -1.2% to +1.0%. GSM8K (256) was 243 vs 246 and 244 vs 245 (fixed 3 first). - Before the fallback, the stop ran at every batch size and was 5.2% slower than fixed 3 at c=4; the fallback removes that. - Summarization regresses in every run (-3.7% to -9.0%). - The gain needs a cheap draft step: with the stock BF16 draft head the stop gains only +2.3% over 3 drafts.
Per category, c=1 (tok/s / AL) | category | Fixed 3 drafts | Confidence stop, max 6 | stop vs best fixed | |---|---:|---:|---:| | coding | 62.1 / 3.61 | 72.4 / 5.14 | +16.7% | | humanities | 42.9 / 2.50 | 42.0 / 2.40 | -2.1% | | math | 51.1 / 2.99 | 53.2 / 3.22 | +4.2% | | multilingual | 52.5 / 3.02 | 54.0 / 3.44 | +2.8% | | qa | 48.9 / 2.76 | 49.3 / 2.93 | +0.8% | | rag | 54.1 / 2.92 | 58.9 / 3.43 | +9.0% | | reasoning | 45.6 / 2.59 | 45.6 / 2.57 | +0.0% | | roleplay | 46.3 / 2.50 | 46.8 / 2.58 | +0.9% | | stem | 43.1 / 2.49 | 42.2 / 2.47 | -2.0% | | summarization | 49.4 / 2.88 | 45.6 / 3.01 | -7.7% | | writing | 44.7 / 2.50 | 45.5 / 2.57 | +1.8% | | average | 49.1 / 2.80 | 50.5 / 3.07 | +2.7% |
## Design questions raised on earlier attempts (#35301, #43522, #44885) - **Host sync.** The stop reads its chain flag after each draft step, but only when one request is decoding; with more requests there is no readback. On GB200 the readback made decode 24.7% slower (fixed 6: 378.4, stop: 284.8 tok/s), which is why it is SM121 only. A sync-free version is not cheap: about 65% of the gain is the shorter verify, so the host needs the drafted count, and reading it once per round was just as slow on GB200 (286.8). CUDA graph IF nodes can skip draft steps on the device (about 15 us each), but a device-side verify would need a switch over per-length verify graphs and device-side input preparation. - **Variable verify length.** Each verify length 1..K has its own FULL graph at batch size 1 (larger batches keep only the fallback and full lengths), so a shorter verify never replays a graph captured for another shape. Cost here: 13 FULL graphs instead of 5, 0.65 vs 0.45 GiB graph memory, capture time unchanged. Attention backends that only take an optimized path at a fixed spec-token count may run slower at the shorter lengths; this was measured with Qwen4Exp QSA/GDN only. - **Baselines and data.** Compared against the best fixed depth from a same-node sweep, on SPEED-Bench, not synthetic or ShareGPT prompts. - **Gains at higher batch.** The mean chain length flattens with batch size, so the stop only runs at one request. - **Hardware specific.** Yes: it helps where a draft step is long, which is why it is gated. SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090) is untested. ## Not a duplicate - #35301 (same knob) and #28693 were closed as stale; #43522 and #44885 (confidence-based verify truncation for DFlash/PARD) were closed. - #52228 trims verify width from an online estimator and needs varlen attention backends, which Qwen4Exp QSA/GDN lack; it does not stop drafting. #52559 picks a per-step K for DFlash from past averages and reports no gain at c=1. - #32374 (Dynamic SD) picks K per batch-size range; at c=1 that is the fixed-depth baseline. Once its MTP drafter capture fix lands (#58821), a Dynamic SD schedule could drive the fallback depth instead of a separate key. ## Tests ```bash pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_confidence_stop.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k confidence_stop ``` On GB10, at 7c4775ff31: 41 unit tests passed, and the e2e test passed (Qwen3.5-0.8B MTP, one request at a time, greedy outputs match fixed-depth MTP, AL at least 0.9x fixed 3). pre-commit and the mypy manual stage are clean. The serving numbers come from this branch applied with #59973 to a nightly 0cbac6cd1-based image. Size: about 220 source lines (84 in the new `confidence_stop.py`, 39 of config validation), 255 test lines, 7 doc lines. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above. **Reproduction on upstream main (DGX Spark, GB10)** Upstream main 02b83919aa with the heads of #59958, #59973, #59740, #60068 and #54614 merged, no other runtime patches. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 6 with confidence stop 0.6, sparse draft head via `draft_token_map` (32k ids, 16384 dynamic rows at rank 256, `draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), FP8 KV, `host_file_gather` PLE tables. SPEED-Bench throughput 2K in / 1K out, fixed OSL, c=1, n=20: | Build | tok/s/user | AL | GSM8K-256 | |---|---|---|---| | upstream main + these PRs | 49.94 | 2.68 | 249/256 | | our internal stack, same node | 49.73 | 2.65 | 245/256 | The PR route reproduces the internal stack result within noise.

SM120 data for the "untested" line, with the gate widened locally to SM12x (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, main `153a17166e`, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with the stock BF16 MTP head and the checkpoint's FP8 KV, SPEED-Bench qualitative 44 prompts, greedy, 256 tokens, one autotune file pinned across arms): at c=1 the stop (max 6, threshold 0.6, fallback 3) raises acceptance length from 3.02 to 3.16 but makes median TPOT 12.3% worse than fixed 3 (9.31 against 8.29 ms, two boots each, separated), fixed 6 is 3.2% worse (one boot), and the PR with the stop off is within 0.4% of main (one boot). On main `153a17166e` the e2e test also misses its acceptance-length bound (2.122 against 0.9 x 2.430), so with the BF16 head, keeping it SM121-only is right for this card.

Thanks for the reproduction section. We are trying to match its throughput-2K row (49.94 tok/s/user, AL 2.68) on our own DGX Spark and land lower. Three questions would help us close it out:

1. **Are the dense (non-expert) layers BF16 in your run?** "No other runtime patches" suggests so. On our build, BF16 dense layers cost about 24% of decode (stop 0.7 rows below), while your figure implies 18.6 verification rounds per second (49.94 ÷ 2.68). That is close to our build with dense layers cast to FP8 (17.8-20.2 over 13 runs: stop 0.5-0.7 and our KV and RecoverSSM variants) and well above our BF16-dense runs (14.7-15.5 over 4 runs).
2. **How is tok/s/user computed?** On our runs, the mean of per-request rates (output tokens ÷ (latency − mean TTFT)) reads 3-11% higher than 1000 / mean TPOT.
3. **Which checkpoint revision and harness command?** We use `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ `fc694b54` and `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name speed_bench --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --num-prompts 20 --max-concurrency 1 --disable-shuffle --ignore-eos`, with `--temperature 0` for the greedy runs. A difference in endpoint (chat template), shuffling, EOS handling or sampling could explain part of the gap.

What we measure on one GB10: the 20 prompts reconstructed from your sample (the 5 AdaLEval rows from a third-party Hub copy, `huyyeuai/speed_bench`, because the AdaLEval host was unreachable from our network), c=1, 1K fixed output, one boot per arm. All arms run MTP 6 with the same sparse draft head (32k ids, 16,384 dynamic rows, rank 256, NVFP4) and fallback depth 3, which our port of this PR requires with a threshold and which has no effect at c=1.

| Our build | tok/s (1000 / mean TPOT) | AL |
|---|---|---|
| Stop 0.7, dense FP8, greedy ×4; sampled ×1 | 48.41, 46.00, 44.90, 46.12; 44.65 | 2.45, 2.28, 2.22, 2.32; 2.28 |
| Stop 0.6, dense FP8, greedy ×2 | 44.70, 46.22 | 2.38, 2.43 |
| Stop 0.7, dense BF16, greedy ×2 | 33.82, 35.16 | 2.18, 2.31 |
| Stop 0.6, dense BF16, FP8 KV on the MTP layer too, without RecoverSSM (#58863), greedy ×2 | 34.40, 35.08 | 2.34, 2.34 |

Across 16 runs on this prompt set, AL is 2.15-2.45. Our build is a 2026-10-16 vLLM nightly with this PR (ported at 029a811e), #59740, #59973 (its quantized draft head off in these runs), our port of #58815 for the PLE path instead of #59958, and other patches, not main 02b83919, so it is not an exact replica: the PR heads no longer apply cleanly to current main. Happy to share the result JSONs.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the thorough writeup and measurements. My main concern is the maintenance cost relative to the scope. The PR touches several shared paths (model runner input prep, cudagraph capture candidates, base and autoregressive speculators) for a gain limited to c=1 on SM121. `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and the surrounding MRV2 paths are already complex, and every future optimization/feature that lands there will have to keep this one working. As it stands, I don't think the tradeoff is worth it. I'd be more comfortable if the approach generalized to more concurrencies and hardware, and the changes were more localized.

Perhaps we can take a different direction where we instead add varlen support to the QSA/GDN backends, and leverage AV to handle the trimming for us? AV currently uses stale confidence scores to decide on the batch size. For low-concurrency cases where a sync pays off (e.g. SM121 at c=1), we could extend AV with an opt-in mode that reads the fresh confidences. That would still be hardware-specific, but contained to AV rather than spread through the runner. Just an idea.

Stopping drafting early is trickier, since we're pushing `TargetDependentARSpeculator` toward fusing the last N-1 decode steps, and this PR currently disables fused decode whenever the feature is enabled. CUDA graph conditional nodes inside the fused graph might be a sync-free way to do it (you mentioned measuring ~15 µs per step), but I'd explore that separately, after the target-side trimming.

files.patch:
@@ -74,3 +74,10 @@ vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-7B-Base \
   is a good default to start with.
 - If your model does not support MTP, use another method such as EAGLE or draft
   model speculation.
+- `"draft_confidence_threshold": 0.6` with `"draft_confidence_fallback_depth": 3`
+  (Model Runner V2, SM121 GPUs such as DGX Spark) makes `num_speculative_tokens`
+  a maximum depth while one request is decoding: drafting stops once its next
+  draft is not that confident, and only the drafted prefix is verified. With
+  more requests it drafts the fallback depth instead. It waits on the GPU after
+  every draft step, which costs more than it saves on faster GPUs, so it is
+  rejected elsewhere; SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090) is untested.

@@ -2090,6 +2090,43 @@ def test_per_request_spec_decode_subtracts_invalid_drafts():
     assert payload["acceptance_histogram"] == [0, 0, 1, 0]
 
 
+def test_spec_decode_stats_count_only_verified_drafts():
+    """When the runner verifies fewer drafts than scheduled, only those count
+    as proposed, while the rejection rollback still covers every placeholder."""
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        num_speculative_tokens=3, per_request_spec_decode_metrics="detailed"
+    )
+    [req] = create_requests(num_requests=1, num_tokens=1)
+    scheduler.add_request(req)
+    rid = req.request_id
+
+    def _mk_output(sampled, num_verified=None):
+        return ModelRunnerOutput(
+            req_ids=[rid],
+            req_id_to_index={rid: 0},
+            sampled_token_ids=[sampled],
+            num_verified_spec_tokens=num_verified,
+        )
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler.schedule(), _mk_output([0]))
+    scheduler.update_draft_token_ids(DraftTokenIds([rid], [[1, 2, 3]]))
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    # 3 scheduled, 2 verified, 1 accepted.
+    engine_core_outputs = scheduler.update_from_output(
+        output, _mk_output([1, 9], num_verified=[2])
+    )
+
+    stats = engine_core_outputs[0].scheduler_stats.spec_decoding_stats
+    assert stats.num_drafts == 1
+    assert stats.num_draft_tokens == 2
+    assert stats.num_accepted_tokens == 1
+    assert stats.num_draft_tokens_per_pos == [1, 1, 0]
+    payload = req.spec_decode_metrics.to_dict()
+    assert payload["per_step_drafted"] == [2]
+    assert payload["per_step_accepted"] == [1]
+    assert req.num_computed_tokens == 1 + 4 - 2
+
+
 def test_per_request_spec_decode_acceptance_disabled_by_default():
     scheduler = create_scheduler(num_speculative_tokens=3)
     assert scheduler.spec_decode_metrics_level == "none"

@@ -5,7 +5,14 @@
 
 from tests.utils import single_gpu_only
 from vllm import SamplingParams
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 
+from ...utils import (
+    assert_request_outputs_match,
+    compute_acceptance_len,
+    get_spec_decode_metric_value,
+    get_test_prompts,
+)
 from .._correctness import check_mtp_correctness
 
 
@@ -37,3 +44,58 @@ def test_mtp_correctness(
         expected_accuracy_threshold,
         vllm_runner,
     )
+
+
+@single_gpu_only
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability(121)),
+    reason="draft_confidence_threshold is SM121 only",
+)
+def test_mtp_draft_confidence_stop(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    sampling_config: SamplingParams,
+    vllm_runner,
+):
+    """The stop only shortens drafting: greedy outputs match fixed-depth MTP,
+    a deeper capped chain keeps at least 90% of the fixed chain's AL, and the
+    draft counters count only verified drafts. One request at a time, so the
+    stop rather than the fallback is used."""
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER", "1")
+    prompts = get_test_prompts(mm_enabled=False, num_prompts=32)
+    results = {}
+    drafts_per_round = {}
+    for num_spec, threshold in ((3, None), (4, 0.6)):
+        with vllm_runner(
+            "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base",
+            block_size=None,
+            enable_chunked_prefill=None,

+def _logits(top_probs: list[float]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """bf16 rows whose top-1 probability is approximately each value."""
+    rows = torch.full((len(top_probs), VOCAB), -30.0)
+    for row, p in enumerate(top_probs):
+        rows[row, 5] = 0.0
+        rows[row, VOCAB - 3] = rows[row, VOCAB - 9000] = float(
+            np.log((1 - p) / (2 * p))
+        )
+    return rows.to(device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _run_step(stop, top_probs, step):
+    stop.update(_logits(top_probs), torch.tensor([step], device="cuda"))
+    stop.step_launched()
+

+    stop = DraftConfidenceStop(THRESHOLD, FALLBACK, 8, NUM_STEPS, torch.device("cuda"))

+    # Only the first row is the request; the second is cudagraph padding.
+    _run_step(stop, [0.9, 0.1], 0)
+    assert stop.should_continue()
+    _run_step(stop, [0.7, 0.1], 1)
+    assert stop.should_continue()
+    _run_step(stop, [0.4, 0.99], 2)
+    assert not stop.should_continue()
+    # Steps 0 and 1 cleared the threshold; step 2's draft did not.
+    assert stop.num_verifiable_drafts(np.array([3])).tolist() == [2]

+    assert not stop.alive.item()
+    stop.begin_round(1)
+    _run_step(stop, [0.99], 0)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import math
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug import gpu_sync_allowed
+
+
+class DraftConfidenceStop:
+    """Ends a single request's draft round once a draft's top-1 probability
+    falls below the threshold; the first draft is always kept."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        threshold: float,
+        fallback_depth: int,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        num_steps: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ):
+        self.fallback_depth = fallback_depth
+        self.num_steps = num_steps
+        self.log_threshold = math.log(threshold)
+        self.alive = torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+        self._alive_cpu = torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.bool, pin_memory=True)
+        self._alive_ready = torch.cuda.Event()
+        # Verifiable drafts per request-state slot, from its last draft round.
+        self._num_drafts_np = np.full(max_num_reqs, num_steps, dtype=np.int32)
+        self._slot: int | None = None
+        # A round that ran every step; its last step is read when next needed.
+        self._pending_slot: int | None = None
+        self._steps_launched = 0
+
+    def update(self, logits: torch.Tensor, draft_step: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        """Fold the first row's draft confidence into the chain (graph-safe)."""
+        row = logits[:1].float()
+        confident = (row.amax(-1) - row.logsumexp(-1)) >= self.log_threshold
+        self.alive.copy_(confident & (self.alive | (draft_step == 0)))
+
+    def begin_round(self, slot: int) -> None:
+        self._resolve_pending()
+        self._slot = slot
+        self._steps_launched = 0
+
+    def fixed_round(self, slots: np.ndarray, num_drafts: int) -> None:
+        self._resolve_pending()
+        self._num_drafts_np[slots] = num_drafts
+        self._slot = None
+
+    def step_launched(self) -> None:
+        self._steps_launched += 1
+        self._alive_cpu.copy_(self.alive, non_blocking=True)
+        self._alive_ready.record()
+
+    def _read_alive(self) -> bool:
+        with gpu_sync_allowed():
+            self._alive_ready.synchronize()
+        return bool(self._alive_cpu[0])
+
+    def should_continue(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the chain survived the last launched step. Waits for it."""
+        if self._read_alive():
+            return True
+        assert self._slot is not None
+        self._num_drafts_np[self._slot] = max(1, self._steps_launched - 1)
+        self._slot = None
+        return False
+
+    def end_round(self) -> None:
+        """Close a round that launched every step, without waiting for it."""
+        self._pending_slot, self._slot = self._slot, None
+
+    def _resolve_pending(self) -> None:
+        if self._pending_slot is not None:
+            survived = self._read_alive()
+            self._num_drafts_np[self._pending_slot] = self.num_steps - (not survived)
+            self._pending_slot = None
+
+    def num_verifiable_drafts(self, slots: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        """Drafts each request may verify, from its slot's last draft round."""
+        self._resolve_pending()
+        return self._num_drafts_np[slots]

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the thorough writeup and measurements. My main concern is the maintenance cost relative to the scope. The PR touches several shared paths (model runner input prep, cudagraph capture candidates, base and autoregressive speculators) for a gain limited to c=1 on SM121. `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and the surrounding MRV2 paths are already complex, and every future optimization/feature that lands there will have to keep this one working. As it stands, I don't think the tradeoff is worth it. I'd be more comfortable if the approach generalized to more concurrencies and hardware, and the changes were more localized.

Perhaps we can take a different direction where we instead add varlen support to the QSA/GDN backends, and leverage AV to handle the trimming for us? AV currently uses stale confidence scores to decide on the batch size. For low-concurrency cases where a sync pays off (e.g. SM121 at c=1), we could extend AV with an opt-in mode that reads the fresh confidences. That would still be hardware-specific, but contained to AV rather than spread through the runner. Just an idea.

Stopping drafting early is trickier, since we're pushing `TargetDependentARSpeculator` toward fusing the last N-1 decode steps, and this PR currently disables fused decode whenever the feature is enabled. CUDA graph conditional nodes inside the fused graph might be a sync-free way to do it (you mentioned measuring ~15 µs per step), but I'd explore that separately, after the target-side trimming.
